the bond strength between FRP and epoxy deteriorates with time under moisture exposure, and the deterioration rate can be quantified by fracture toughness.
moisture can cause irreversible weakening of concrete/epoxy bond strength and that this weakening can be quantified and used to predict the service life of FRPs.

the long-term durability issues of FRP strengthening systems under moisture cyclic exposure, and the proposed approach is expected to be useful for the design and service life prediction of FRP strengthening system for concrete structures.

the moisture condition is one of the key parameters affecting the long-term performance and service life of FRPs, which should be taken into account in the design of FRP retrofit system.
the moisture degradation in the bond system is a function of both moisture content and the number of moisture cycles.
moisture cyclic condition can significantly reduce bond strength of FRP-concrete bond system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tri-layer fracture test can be used as a tool for the durability assessment of FRP-strengthed concrete structures.
, moisture is a key factor affecting the durability of the FRP/concrete interface.
moisture degradation of FRP/conrete bond system can be quantified by fracture toughness, and the service life of the FRP strengthening system could be estimated by a proposed model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
moisture can cause irreversible weakening in the bond system.
moisture degradation of FRP-strengthened concrete structure can be quantified by fracture toughness.
